question: Will the September 2026 US jobs report show nonfarm payrolls rose by more than 100,000?

calls.reasoning: 2026's true payroll run rate is ~80k/month (RBC; Sept 2026 FOMC statement), not the 31k trailing-12-month figure the background quotes, which is dragged by a very weak 2025 H2. Centering September's first print near 70-80k with a residual SD of ~90k (2026 first-print residuals; consensus-error SD ~100k) puts >100k at roughly 36-40%. Pushing up: 5 of 8 2026 first prints exceeded 100k, claims are at 196k with continuing claims the lowest since Jan-2024, Challenger Jan-Aug cuts the lowest since 2022, federal cuts down 92% y/y, diffusion index highest since Dec-2024. Pushing down: the 100k threshold sits above both trend and any plausible consensus (~50-60k), the >100k months clustered in the stronger Jan-May stretch (3-month trend is 71k), and TD flags August's leisure/hospitality and local-government gains plus a freak +35k federal print as overstated and reversion-prone. Kalshi's exact-terms contract (same threshold, same initial-print instrument, closes at release) trades 0.38/0.44, last 0.45, ~16.7k contracts; I sit just above its mid. Release risk is negligible - the Oct 1 shutdown was averted by a CR through Dec 11.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off the seasonally adjusted over-the-month change in total nonfarm payroll employment for September 2026 as printed in the INITIAL BLS Employment Situation release (2026-10-02 13:00Z / 8:30am ET), not the revised figure, not private trackers, not the household survey. Threshold is strictly greater than +100,000; +100,000 exactly resolves NO. Delay past the window annuls.

EVENT WINDOW: the measured quantity is the payroll level change from the pay period including Aug 12, 2026 to the pay period including Sep 12, 2026 per CES methodology implied by the criteria. That September reference period closed on 2026-09-12, i.e. 100% of the measured interval had already elapsed as of Now (2026-09-22T09:37Z); only collection, seasonal adjustment and publication remain.

EVIDENCE
- Aug 2026 print (BLS, rel. 2026-09-04): +162,000, vs Dow Jones consensus 53-55k; unemployment 4.1%; participation 61.6%; avg hourly earnings +0.3% m/m, +3.1% y/y.
- Same release: June revised +20k->+31k, July revised -23k->+21k (net +55k upward revision to the prior two months).
- Aug composition (BLS / TD Economics, Sep 2026): leisure & hospitality +62k (food services +59k), local government +50k (local gov education +42k), health care & social assistance +28k, construction +22k, manufacturing +16k, information -23k, federal government +35k. TD Economics wrote that the leisure & hospitality and local-government strength was "likely overstated."
- Diffusion index 55.6% in August, highest since Dec 2024 (TD Economics, Sep 2026).
- 3-month average payroll gain rose to 71k in August from 38k in July (TD Economics).
- 2026 first prints by data month (investing.com economic calendar, actual vs consensus): Jan +130 vs 66; Feb -92 vs 58; Mar +178 vs 65; Apr +115 vs 65; May +172 vs 85; Jun +57 vs 114; Jul -23 vs 85; Aug +162 vs 55. Dec 2025: +50 vs 66.
- Current-vintage PAYEMS monthly changes 2026 (FRED, pulled 2026-09-22): Jan +160, Feb -156, Mar +214, Apr +148, May +63, Jun +31, Jul +21, Aug +162. Sep-Dec 2025: +76, -140, +41, -17.
- Initial jobless claims: 196,000 for the week ending 2026-09-12 (down 10k from 206k); 4-week average ~206k; continuing claims fell 39k to 1,730,000, lowest since January 2024 (DOL weekly claims).
- Challenger, Gray & Christmas (Aug 2026 report): 52,881 announced cuts in August, up from 33,429 in July but -38.5% y/y and the lowest August since 2022; Jan-Aug total 529,914, -41% y/y, lowest Jan-Aug since 2022; government-announced cuts 1,477 in August, 22,229 YTD, -92% vs 295,273 through Aug 2025.
- ADP National Employment Report (rel. 2026-09-02): private employment +38,000 in August, below the 47k estimate and down from 46k in July, slowest since January. September ADP is scheduled for 2026-09-30, i.e. after this writing and before resolution.
- FOMC 2026-09-16 raised the funds target to 3.75-4.00%, first hike since July 2023, unanimous; statement/coverage cited the economy "near maximum employment," unemployment 4.1%, "employers adding an average of 80,000 jobs each month this year," and claims near all-time lows; inflation above target was the stated driver.
- RBC Economics (2026-09-21): 2026 average monthly job gains ~80,000 vs under 10,000/month in 2025; estimated breakeven employment pace ~20,000/month (St. Louis Fed range 15k-87k) because of retirements and slowed immigration; layoffs near all-time lows; labor force shrinking; aggregate weekly hours +1.2% y/y.
- Release risk: the Oct 1, 2026 funding lapse was averted - a continuing resolution passed the Senate 90-6 and the House 370-48 and was signed 2026-09-02, funding the government through Dec 11, 2026. No BLS publication blackout is pending for the Oct 2 release.
- Labor actions in September 2026 were small and localized (1,300 Encore Boston Harbor casino workers; a one-day West Anaheim Medical Center nurses strike Sep 3-4; a strike-authorization vote, not a strike, at SEIU Local 1000 in California). A viral claim of a nationwide trucker strike starting Oct 1 was debunked (Snopes, 2026-09-17). No large national work stoppage overlapped the Sep 6-12 reference week. For contrast, a health-care strike is the widely cited cause of the Feb 2026 negative print.

BASE RATES (with the class each is computed over)
- Over the 8 data-months of 2026, first prints exceeding +100k: 5 of 8 (Jan, Mar, Apr, May, Aug). Mean first print 87k, median ~122k; SD of first prints around an 80k trend ~90k.
- Over the 12 data-months through Aug 2026 (i.e. including the weak Sep-Dec 2025 stretch), first prints exceeding +100k: roughly 6 of 12; the trailing 12-month average gain stated by BLS in the August release was +31k.
- Over the 3 most recent data-months only (Jun, Jul, Aug 2026): 1 of 3 first prints exceeded +100k; average of the three revised values 71k.
- Conditional on the prior month printing above +150k (Mar->Apr, May->Jun within 2026): the following month exceeded +100k in 1 of 2 cases.
- Consensus-error class (2026 data-months): actual minus consensus mean about +6k, SD about 100k; individual errors ranged -150k to +113k.

BOTH DIRECTIONS
- For a high print: 2026 run rate ~80k with a ~20k breakeven; claims and continuing claims at multi-year lows; announced layoffs at four-year lows; federal-sector drag has collapsed versus 2025; broad-based August hiring (diffusion 55.6%); persistent pattern of large upside surprises versus consensus in 2026; recent revisions have been upward.
- For a low print: the threshold sits above both the 2026 trend and every consensus figure located; August's gain was concentrated in three reversion-prone components (food services +59k, local government education +42k, federal +35k); ADP private hiring is running 38-47k; the 2026 series is bimodal, with three of eight months printing between -92k and +57k; September's seasonal factors for education hiring are historically among the noisiest of the year; the labor force is shrinking and the Fed has just tightened.

SEARCHED BUT NOT FOUND
- No publish
calls.reference_class: Monthly first-print (as-first-reported) seasonally adjusted change in US total nonfarm payrolls, over the 12 data-months through August 2026, asked whether the print exceeded +100k

calls.reasoning: Reference class: monthly BLS first-print nonfarm payroll changes in 2026 (Jan-Aug). At least 4 of 8 first prints exceeded +100k (Mar ~178k, Apr ~115k, May 172k, Aug 162k), against weak prints in Jun (+20k), Jul (-23k) and Feb — a bimodal distribution with little mass in the 70-140k middle, so the base rate near 50% is the right anchor, not the trailing 12-month average of +31k. Three forces pull that down for September: Capital Economics forecasts +50k; ADP's August private gain of 38k was the slowest since January; and August's beat was concentrated in food services (+59k vs 12k avg) and local government education (+42k), both classic candidates for seasonal payback. Pulling up: initial claims 196k (week to Sept 12), near July's 60-year low of 189k, continuing claims at a two-year low, Challenger Jan-Aug cuts down 41% to the lowest since 2022 with government cuts down 92%, a low break-even pace (~20k, RBC/St. Louis Fed), and a Street consensus that has been badly biased in 2026 (Aug surprise +109k, May +92k). A liquid, exactly-matching Kalshi contract (>100,000, first print, Sept reference month, confirmed against the settled Aug series) prices 0.38/0.43 with last 0.45 on 16.7k volume. My consensus-plus-surprise-SD model gives ~33%, my first-print base rate ~48%; the market sits between them, so I land essentially at the market mid with a small downward tilt for the August-composition payback.

EVIDENCE — FIRMER SIDE:
- Initial jobless claims fell 10,000 to 196,000 in the week ended Sept 12, 2026, the least since the 60-year low of 189,000 in July; continuing claims fell 39,000 to 1,730,000, lowest since January 2024 (Bloomberg, 2026-09-17). A later week ending Sept 21 came in at 218,000 versus a 225,000 consensus.

- Unemployment has fallen from a 2026 high of 4.4% to 4.1% as job growth outpaced labor-supply growth; labor force participation rose 0.2pp in August (PNC Economics, 2026-09-04).

- Forecaster misses in 2026 have been large in both directions: August actual +162k vs Dow Jones consensus +53k (+109k surprise); May actual +172k vs consensus +80k (+92k surprise); June and July both printed far below consensus. Reported August forecaster range spanned roughly -25k to +121k.

calls.reconciliation: Three factual disputes were settled from the dossiers. (1) Count of 2026 first prints above +100k: Runs 1 and 3 independently retrieved Jan-26 = +130k from the investing.com release history, giving 5 of 8; Run 2 said 'at least 4 of 8' and explicitly recorded Jan/Feb first prints as not found. Two independent retrievals over one non-retrieval: 5 of 8, so Run 2's base-rate anchor was slightly low. (2) The 'Capital Economics +50,000 September' forecast that Run 2 weighted as a live downward force: Runs 1 and 3 each independently traced the identical 'continued slimming of the federal workforce' wording to September 2025-vintage content. Not applicable to this question; no published Street median or whisper number for the September 2026 reference month exists yet on any run's search (consensus typically firms Sept 28-Oct 1). This removes one of Run 2's three stated downward forces. (3) Market: all three located the same Kalshi/Robinhood contract, and Run 2 verified its terms against the same series' settled August contract, which settled on the 162k print, so threshold, reference month, initial-print rule and close all match this question. Runs 1 and 2 agree the quote is ~0.38/0.44 on ~16.7k volume; Run 3 observed a non-monotone strike ladder, so I treat the mid (~0.41), not the 0.45 last trade, as the market read. No Polymarket or Manifold contract exists. I retrieved nothing myself on this run, hence empty sources. UNSETTLED: the magnitude of the August composition payback is pure judgment — every run sees the same +59k food services and +42k local-government-education concentration and the same late-Labor-Day calendar, and nothing in the dossiers fixes how much reverses in September; no run found the September 2026 seasonal-factor detail for local government education. I take the reading I would bet on: a real but partial reversal, leaving a central first print of ~80-85k. I carry forward Run 3's first-print reference class (which Runs 1 and 3 share) because the resolving instrument is explicitly the first print, and first prints in 2026 both averaged above the revised series (+87k vs +80k) and were more dispersed, which modestly raises P(>100k) for a center below the threshold. Net, the two settled factual points cut toward YES relative to the pool's lower members while the composition mechanism cuts toward NO, landing me at the top of the runs' range rather than beyond it.
